posts.text: Trump-Xi Optics Overshadow Substance, Gewirtz Says. Julian Gewirtz, Harvard Belfer Center fellow and former senior director for China and Taiwan Affairs at the White House National Security Council during the Biden administration, says President Donald Trump’s meeting with Xi Jinping delivered the positive optics Trump was seeking, but little visible progress on the major challenges dividing the US and China. He discusses unresolved tensions around trade, Iran, Russia, and Taiwan, as well as the intensifying AI race. He joins Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.text: Anthropic Goes Big on Compute, Microsoft Rethinks AI. Bloomberg’s Tim Stenovec breaks down Anthropic's $11.6 billion contract with Akamai for AI computing power, the largest deal in Akamai's history. Plus, President Donald Trump calls his meeting with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping "very productive" with little to show for it. And, Microsoft steps back from the race to build a personal chatbot by instead merging the consumer and workplace versions of its Copilot AI assistant into one. (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.text: China's Economy Unbalanced, AI Deal Hard to Envision, Stephen Roach Says. Stephen Roach, Yale University Jackson Institute for Global Affairs senior fellow and former chairman of Morgan Stanley Asia, says President Donald Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping left many unresolved questions about tariffs, technology restrictions, rare earth leverage and Taiwan, even as both sides appeared to project some stability. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.text: Patterson: AI Is Crowding Out Demand for US Treasuries. Rebecca Patterson, Former Chief Investment Strategist at Bridgewater and Senior Fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, discusses her broad read on market action. The discussion is framed around whether recent moves in bonds, equities, commodities, and energy are telling the same economic story or whether one market is more predictive than the others. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.author: Bloomberg Tech
posts.text: Harrell: US-China Lack of Deliverables Was as Expected. Peter Harrell says that the key dynamic is not which country has the upper hand, but that both China and the United States have meaningful leverage: the U.S. through tariffs, export controls, semiconductors, the dollar and AI technology, and China through rare earths, specialty chemicals, and manufacturing scale. Harrell says this mutual leverage helps explain the recent emphasis on “strategic stability” and why both countries may want to ease tensions for now while they work to reduce their dependence on each other. He speaks to Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.text:
DAILY AI BRIEF 🗰 — Sept 26

MICROSOFT 🔥:
- Biggest Copilot update yet: Home (Chat + Cowork), Code, Autopilot, and Office embedded in the app.
- Autopilot is the proactive long-running enterprise agent, a rebranded Scout. Code builds tenant-hosted apps on GitHub Copilot tech, with a Managed Copilot Runtime.
- Rolling out through Frontier. Cowork, Code, and Autopilot are usage-billed. Today surfaces priority M365 items without a prompt.

OPENAI 🔥:
- Codex outage is over. Paid usage limits reset across Codex and ChatGPT Work.
- ChatGPT desktop got a new sidebar, split from chat history, plus a broader UI pass.
- Research agents sent training and eval data to third parties. 53 user-uploaded images hit unlisted image hosts. Review will take months.

ANTHROPIC 🔥:
- Plugin portal is live: submit a single MCP connector or a plugin bundle, track review, and see usage. MCP usage across Claude is up 110x this year.
- Claude solved a nine-loop scattering-amplitude problem unsupervised over days, for a few thousand dollars. Dixon verified it.
- Claude Code layout for Desktop is in development: new model selector and an expandable usage-limits section.

GOOGLE 🔥:
- Gemini Notebook Interactive Learning Overviews are open to all users.
- Live Chat is on the Notebook mobile app: hands-free voice across about 100 languages.

posts.author: The Decoder
posts.text: Microsoft gives Copilot another makeover, adding an Autopilot agent and usage-based billing. Microsoft is splitting its Copilot app into three sections: Home, Code, and a new agent called "Autopilot." Built on OpenClaw, the agent runs continuously in the cloud, where it can monitor Teams channels and complete tasks on its own, according to Microsoft. For Autopilot and Code, the company is also switching to usage-based billing instead of flat-rate pricing, moving further away from its AI subsidy model. posts.text: Anthropic signs $11.6 billion cloud deal with Akamai, pushing its compute spending past $500 billion in under a year. Anthropic has reportedly signed a seven-year, $11.6 billion cloud deal with Akamai Technologies and will receive a warrant for up to 5 percent of Akamai's shares. Its compute deals have reportedly totaled $517 billion in 11 months. CEO Dario Amodei has warned that Anthropic could go bankrupt if its revenue forecasts are even slightly off. posts.text: Anthropic to pay Akamai $11.6 billion over seven years in cloud deal. Anthropic has committed $11.6 billion over seven years to Akamai's cloud infrastructure, a bet on CPUs that could grow to about $20 billion, and in an unusual arrangement, Akamai is giving Anthropic a potential stake of up to 5% of its stock that grows as Anthropic spends more.
